transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose what brings me in is that I’m frightened of what happens when I start eating. It’s not just, you know, having a bit more than I meant to. It feels like something gets away from me. Once I start, my hands just keep going back for more, and I’m sitting there thinking, Tom, stop this now, you’ve had enough, just stop — but I don’t. It’s like the thought is there, plain as day, but it doesn’t seem to reach my hands somehow.

And I know that probably sounds strange, especially at my age, but it’s been scaring me. I don’t feel in charge in those moments, and that’s the part that made me think I’d better talk to someone rather than just keep pretending I can handle it on my own.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after one of these eating episodes?

Yes… yes, I do. I’m ashamed to say it, but there are times after I’ve eaten too much where I go straight to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. It’s not every single bite or anything like that, but when I feel I’ve gone too far, I get this awful panic that the food is just sitting there inside me, and I can’t settle.

And I’ve taken laxatives too, for the same reason, really. I get scared the food will stay in me, and I tell myself I’m just trying to undo it somehow. I know that probably sounds terrible, especially saying it out loud, but yes… I have done that.
How often do these episodes of eating too much happen?

I’ve tried to work that out, actually, because I knew if I came in here and just said “a lot,” that wouldn’t help much. I started writing it down in a little notebook—what I ate, when it happened, and what I did afterward—and looking back over it, it’s been going on for many months now.

Nearly every week there’s been at least one afternoon where it gets out of hand. Afternoons seem to be the worst for me. I’ll start eating and then it just keeps going, and afterward I’ll panic and try to make up for it somehow—sometimes by making myself sick, sometimes laxatives, sometimes not eating for a while after, or pushing myself too hard with walking around or doing chores.

So… not every day, no, but it’s not rare either. When I look at the logs, it’s almost every week, at least once, and it’s been that way for quite a while.
Do you worry about gaining weight as a result of these eating episodes?

Yes… very much. More than I like to admit, really. It sounds foolish when I say it out loud, because my doctor has told me I’m too thin, and I do hear that, I do understand the words. But it doesn’t feel that way in my head.

If I get on the scale and it’s up even half a pound, I feel this rush of panic, like I’ve done something wrong. I’ll stand there staring at the number as if it’s proof that I’ve let myself go, even if it’s such a tiny change that anyone else would probably say it means nothing. I feel ashamed, almost dirty with myself, and then I start thinking I have to fix it right away. I can’t just leave it alone and say, “Well, that’s normal,” or “It’s just a fluctuation.” It grabs hold of me.

So yes, after those eating episodes especially, I’m terrified I’ll gain weight from it. It’s not just a passing worry. It feels urgent, like I’ve lost control and need to undo the damage somehow.
Do you think you look overweight even when others tell you that you're too thin?

Yes… I do. I know that probably doesn’t make sense to other people, because my doctor has said straight out that I’m too thin. And I hear it, I really do. I’m not trying to be difficult. But when I look at myself, or when I get on the scale, it doesn’t feel true in my head.

If the number is up even half a pound, I get this awful panicky feeling, like I’ve suddenly let myself go. I feel ashamed, like I’ve done something wrong and I have to fix it right away. It’s not like I can calmly tell myself, “That’s nothing, that’s just normal.” I know other people might see it that way, but I don’t feel it that way. It feels much bigger than it is.
Is your main reason for making yourself vomit or using laxatives after eating too much because you're afraid of gaining weight?

Yes… that is the main reason, I think. I wish I could say it was something else, or that it was just because I felt physically uncomfortable, but really it’s because I get frightened that the food is going to stay in me and turn into weight.

There are times after I’ve eaten too much where I’ll go straight to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. I don’t feel calm about it at all—it’s more like panic, like I have to get rid of it before it “counts,” if that makes sense. And I’ve taken laxatives for the same reason, because I’m scared of the food sitting inside me. It sounds awful saying it plainly, but yes… it’s mostly the fear of gaining weight that makes me do it.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the most important thing when it comes to how you feel about yourself?

Yes… I think it is, though I don’t like admitting that. It feels shameful, especially at my age, to say that a number on a scale or how I think my body looks can decide whether I feel all right with myself or not. But it does.

Even when my doctor tells me I’m too thin, that doesn’t really settle it inside me. If I step on the scale and it’s up even half a pound, I can feel myself change right away. I get panicky, and ashamed, like I’ve let myself go somehow. It’s ridiculous, maybe, because half a pound shouldn’t mean anything, but to me it feels like I’ve failed, like I need to fix it immediately.

So yes, my weight and shape have too much power over how I feel about myself. More than anything else sometimes. It’s like I can’t judge myself fairly unless that number feels “safe,” and if it doesn’t, I feel awful about who I am.
Do you feel that your self-worth is largely defined by your weight and body shape?

Yes… yes, I think that’s fair to say. I don’t like that it’s true, but it is. Even when my doctor tells me I’m too thin, it doesn’t seem to sink in the way it should. I can hear the words, but then I get on the scale and if it’s up even half a pound, everything in me just drops.

I feel panicky, like something has gone terribly wrong, and ashamed too, like I’ve let myself go or lost control somehow. And then it’s not just about the number anymore — it feels like it says something about me, like I’ve failed and I have to fix it right away. I know half a pound probably sounds like nothing, but in my head it feels much bigger than that. So yes… my weight and shape do end up deciding how I feel about myself, more than I wish they did.
How often do you make yourself vomit after eating?

It’s not every single time I eat too much, but… it has been happening regularly. I’ve been keeping food logs, and when I look back at them, for many months now, almost every week has at least one afternoon where I ate out of control and then tried to make up for it somehow.

Sometimes that meant making myself vomit. Other times I used laxatives, or I wouldn’t eat afterward, or I’d push myself with walking and chores until I felt like I’d done something to undo it. But vomiting is part of that pattern, yes. It’s usually after those afternoons when I feel like I’ve lost control, and then I panic and feel like I have to do something right away.
Do you usually try to make up for the extra food after one of these eating episodes by vomiting, using laxatives, or some other way?

Yes… I do. I mean, not every time in exactly the same way, but after those times when I feel I’ve eaten too much, I usually feel this awful panic, like I can’t just let it sit there in me.

There are times I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. I hate saying that out loud, but that is what happens. It’s like I tell myself I’ll feel calmer afterward, or that I’ve undone some of the damage, even though I know that probably sounds strange.

And I’ve taken laxatives too, because I get scared the food will stay in me, or that I’ll gain from it. It’s not even always thought through clearly — it’s more like fear takes over and I’m trying to get rid of it somehow. So yes, I do try to make up for it that way.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating?

Yes… I think it is. I wish I could say it was about feeling sick or uncomfortable after eating, but if I’m being honest, the fear of gaining weight is what really sets it off.

Even when my doctor tells me I’m too thin, that doesn’t reassure me the way it probably should. I’ll hear it, and part of me knows I’m supposed to take that seriously, but then if I step on the scale and it’s up even half a pound, I just… I panic. It feels like I’ve let myself go, like I’ve lost control, and I feel ashamed, almost like I’ve done something wrong.

And once that feeling starts, it’s very hard to sit with it. My mind goes straight to, “I have to fix this right now.” So yes, the vomiting or laxatives are tied to that fear — the fear that the food will make the number go up, or that my body will change. It’s not logical, I know, especially at my age and with the doctor saying what he’s saying, but in the moment it feels terribly urgent.
Do you usually try to make up for the extra food after one of these eating episodes most of the time?

Yes… most of the time, I’d say I do try to make up for it somehow. Not always in the exact same way, but it’s hard for me to just leave it alone afterward.

There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. I don’t like admitting that, but that’s what happens. And other times I’ve taken laxatives, because I get scared the food is just going to stay in me, like I won’t be able to undo it or stop what it might do to my body.

It feels very urgent in the moment, like I have to do something right away. Even if later I feel ashamed or worn out by it, at the time it feels like I can’t calm down unless I try to get rid of it somehow.
Is the fear of gaining weight the only reason you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating too much?

I don’t know if I can say it’s the only reason, because sometimes it all gets mixed together in my head — feeling too full, feeling disgusted with myself, feeling like I’ve done something wrong. But the weight part is the thing underneath it, I think. That’s the part that makes it feel so urgent.

Even when my doctor says I’m too thin, it doesn’t really settle me. I hear him say it, and I can nod and understand it for a moment, but then if I get on the scale and it’s up even half a pound, I feel panicky. Ashamed, really. Like I’ve let myself go, like I’ve lost control somehow. And then my mind just goes straight to, “You have to fix this right now.”

So no, maybe it’s not the only feeling in the moment, but the fear of gaining weight is the main thing driving it. That’s the part I can’t seem to quiet down.
How many times a month do you make yourself vomit after eating?

It’s hard for me to give an exact number, because I don’t always write it down or anything, and honestly I try not to think about it too directly. But it does happen more than just once in a while.

There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. It’s usually when I’m scared the food is going to stay in me and I can’t calm myself down. Some months it feels like it happens several times, maybe more depending on how many of those eating episodes I’ve had. And when I don’t vomit, I’ve also taken laxatives for the same reason — that fear that the food is just sitting there and I need to do something about it.

I’m sorry, I know you asked how many times, and I’m not answering very neatly. I’d say… several times a month at least, but I’d have to really think to count it properly.
Do you make yourself vomit after eating at least once a week?

Yes… yes, at least once a week. I don’t like saying it that plainly, but that’s the truth.

It’s usually after I feel like I’ve eaten too much, when I get that panicky feeling that the food is just going to stay in me. I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. And if I don’t do that, there have been times I’ve used laxatives instead, for the same reason — like I need to get it out of me somehow before I can calm down.

It’s not every single day, but once a week, yes. Sometimes more.
Do you make yourself vomit after eating at least three times a week?

I don’t think it’s usually three times a week just vomiting, if you mean only that. Looking at it that narrowly, I’d have to check myself, because some weeks I may vomit more than once, but I don’t know that it’s three times every week.

But my food logs… they show the pattern better than my memory does. For many months now, nearly every week there’s been at least one afternoon where I ate in this out-of-control way, and then afterward I did something to make up for it. Sometimes that was making myself vomit, yes. Other times it was taking laxatives, or not eating afterward, or pushing myself to walk and keep doing chores until I felt like I’d somehow burned it off or undone it.

So if you’re asking specifically three times a week vomiting, I’m not sure I can honestly say that. But the whole cycle of eating too much and then trying to undo it has been happening very regularly, almost every week, for months.
Do you make yourself vomit after eating more than three times a week on average?

More than three times a week… I don’t know if I can honestly say that as an average, not just for making myself vomit. I know there are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and it’s usually because I get scared that the food is just going to stay in me. It’s like I can’t settle down until I’ve done something about it.

But more than three times a week, specifically vomiting, I’m not sure. Some weeks it may feel close, especially if I’ve had more of those times where I feel I’ve eaten too much, but I don’t want to give you a number that isn’t right.

And I should say, when I don’t vomit, I’ve also taken laxatives for the same reason. It’s that same fear — that the food is still in me and I need to get rid of it somehow. So the behavior is there, yes, but if you mean vomiting more than three times a week on average, I’m not certain I can say yes to that.
Do you make yourself vomit after eating nearly every day?

Nearly every day… no, I don’t think I can say that honestly. Not every day.

There are definitely times after I’ve eaten too much, or felt like I had, when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. It’s hard to admit that, but it happens. It’s like once I get scared the food is going to just sit there inside me, I can’t get the thought out of my head. I start feeling very unsettled, almost desperate, and then vomiting feels like the only way to calm that feeling down.

And there have been times I’ve used laxatives too, for the same reason — that same fear that the food will stay in me unless I do something. But if you’re asking whether I make myself vomit nearly every single day, I don’t think that’s right. It happens, yes, but I wouldn’t call it daily.
Do you make yourself vomit after eating every day?

Every day? No… I don’t think I can say every day. That wouldn’t be honest.

But there are times, after I eat too much or feel like I’ve eaten too much, when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, but that’s what happens. I get frightened that the food is going to stay in me, and then I feel like I have to do something right then, like I can’t just sit with it.

And when I don’t make myself vomit, I’ve also taken laxatives for that same reason. It’s all tied to that fear that the food is still inside me and I need to get it out somehow. But if you mean literally every single day, no, not every day.

doctor.question: Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: Even with my doctor saying I’m too thin, if the scale is up half a pound I feel panicky and ashamed, like I’ve let myself go and have to fix it right away.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether fear of gaining weight is the main motivation behind vomiting or laxative use, which most directly matches Fear_of_Weight_Gain.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think it is. I wish I could say it was about feeling sick or uncomfortable after eating, but if I’m being honest, the fear of gaining weight is what really sets it off.

Even when my doctor tells me I’m too thin, that doesn’t reassure me the way it probably should. I’ll hear it, and part of me knows I’m supposed to take that seriously, but then if I step on the scale and it’s up even half a pound, I just… I panic. It feels like I’ve let myself go, like I’ve lost control, and I feel ashamed, almost like I’ve done something wrong.

And once that feeling starts, it’s very hard to sit with it. My mind goes straight to, “I have to fix this right now.” So yes, the vomiting or laxatives are tied to that fear — the fear that the food will make the number go up, or that my body will change. It’s not logical, I know, especially at my age and with the doctor saying what he’s saying, but in the moment it feels terribly urgent.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's binge eating episodes are followed by compensatory behaviors most of the time
doctor.question: Do you usually try to make up for the extra food after one of these eating episodes most of the time?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and I’ve also taken laxatives because I’m scared the food will stay in me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether you typically compensate after binge-eating episodes; in this dialogue the most direct compensatory behavior discussed is vomiting or laxative use after eating.

patient.answer:
Yes… most of the time, I’d say I do try to make up for it somehow. Not always in the exact same way, but it’s hard for me to just leave it alone afterward.

There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. I don’t like admitting that, but that’s what happens. And other times I’ve taken laxatives, because I get scared the food is just going to stay in me, like I won’t be able to undo it or stop what it might do to my body.

It feels very urgent in the moment, like I have to do something right away. Even if later I feel ashamed or worn out by it, at the time it feels like I can’t calm down unless I try to get rid of it somehow.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's fear of gaining weight is the primary motivator for their purging behavior
doctor.question: Is the fear of gaining weight the only reason you make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating too much?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: Even with my doctor saying I’m too thin, if the scale is up half a pound I feel panicky and ashamed, like I’ve let myself go and have to fix it right away.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the vomiting or laxative use is motivated by fear of gaining weight, which directly matches this symptom.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I can say it’s the only reason, because sometimes it all gets mixed together in my head — feeling too full, feeling disgusted with myself, feeling like I’ve done something wrong. But the weight part is the thing underneath it, I think. That’s the part that makes it feel so urgent.

Even when my doctor says I’m too thin, it doesn’t really settle me. I hear him say it, and I can nod and understand it for a moment, but then if I get on the scale and it’s up even half a pound, I feel panicky. Ashamed, really. Like I’ve let myself go, like I’ve lost control somehow. And then my mind just goes straight to, “You have to fix this right now.”

So no, maybe it’s not the only feeling in the moment, but the fear of gaining weight is the main thing driving it. That’s the part I can’t seem to quiet down.

doctor.question: How many times a month do you make yourself vomit after eating?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and I’ve also taken laxatives because I’m scared the food will stay in me.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about how often I make myself vomit after eating, which is a purging compensatory behavior.

patient.answer:
It’s hard for me to give an exact number, because I don’t always write it down or anything, and honestly I try not to think about it too directly. But it does happen more than just once in a while.

There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. It’s usually when I’m scared the food is going to stay in me and I can’t calm myself down. Some months it feels like it happens several times, maybe more depending on how many of those eating episodes I’ve had. And when I don’t vomit, I’ve also taken laxatives for the same reason — that fear that the food is just sitting there and I need to do something about it.

I’m sorry, I know you asked how many times, and I’m not answering very neatly. I’d say… several times a month at least, but I’d have to really think to count it properly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's self-induced vomiting occurs at least weekly
doctor.question: Do you make yourself vomit after eating at least once a week?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and I’ve also taken laxatives because I’m scared the food will stay in me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about self-induced vomiting after eating, which is a purging compensatory behavior.

patient.answer:
Yes… yes, at least once a week. I don’t like saying it that plainly, but that’s the truth.

It’s usually after I feel like I’ve eaten too much, when I get that panicky feeling that the food is just going to stay in me. I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. And if I don’t do that, there have been times I’ve used laxatives instead, for the same reason — like I need to get it out of me somehow before I can calm down.

It’s not every single day, but once a week, yes. Sometimes more.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's self-induced vomiting occurs frequently enough to meet the diagnostic criteria for bulimia nervosa
doctor.question: Do you make yourself vomit after eating at least three times a week?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: My food logs show that for many months now, nearly every week has had at least one afternoon where I ate out of control and then tried to make up for it by vomiting, laxatives, fasting, or pushing myself with walking and chores.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency of vomiting after eating, specifically whether it occurs at least three times a week. The closest covered profile item about frequency is the additional requirement describing recurrent binge eating and compensatory behaviors occurring at least weekly over several months.

patient.answer:
I don’t think it’s usually three times a week just vomiting, if you mean only that. Looking at it that narrowly, I’d have to check myself, because some weeks I may vomit more than once, but I don’t know that it’s three times every week.

But my food logs… they show the pattern better than my memory does. For many months now, nearly every week there’s been at least one afternoon where I ate in this out-of-control way, and then afterward I did something to make up for it. Sometimes that was making myself vomit, yes. Other times it was taking laxatives, or not eating afterward, or pushing myself to walk and keep doing chores until I felt like I’d somehow burned it off or undone it.

So if you’re asking specifically three times a week vomiting, I’m not sure I can honestly say that. But the whole cycle of eating too much and then trying to undo it has been happening very regularly, almost every week, for months.

doctor.question: Do you make yourself vomit after eating more than three times a week on average?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and I’ve also taken laxatives because I’m scared the food will stay in me.
target_item.reason: The question is specifically about self-induced vomiting after eating, which is a purging compensatory behavior.

patient.answer:
More than three times a week… I don’t know if I can honestly say that as an average, not just for making myself vomit. I know there are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and it’s usually because I get scared that the food is just going to stay in me. It’s like I can’t settle down until I’ve done something about it.

But more than three times a week, specifically vomiting, I’m not sure. Some weeks it may feel close, especially if I’ve had more of those times where I feel I’ve eaten too much, but I don’t want to give you a number that isn’t right.

And I should say, when I don’t vomit, I’ve also taken laxatives for the same reason. It’s that same fear — that the food is still in me and I need to get rid of it somehow. So the behavior is there, yes, but if you mean vomiting more than three times a week on average, I’m not certain I can say yes to that.

doctor.question: Do you make yourself vomit after eating nearly every day?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and I’ve also taken laxatives because I’m scared the food will stay in me.
target_item.reason: The question is specifically about self-induced vomiting after eating, which is a purging compensatory behavior.

patient.answer:
Nearly every day… no, I don’t think I can say that honestly. Not every day.

There are definitely times after I’ve eaten too much, or felt like I had, when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. It’s hard to admit that, but it happens. It’s like once I get scared the food is going to just sit there inside me, I can’t get the thought out of my head. I start feeling very unsettled, almost desperate, and then vomiting feels like the only way to calm that feeling down.

And there have been times I’ve used laxatives too, for the same reason — that same fear that the food will stay in me unless I do something. But if you’re asking whether I make myself vomit nearly every single day, I don’t think that’s right. It happens, yes, but I wouldn’t call it daily.

doctor.question: Do you make yourself vomit after eating every day?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: There are times after I eat too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up, and I’ve also taken laxatives because I’m scared the food will stay in me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about self-induced vomiting after eating, which is a purging compensatory behavior.

patient.answer:
Every day? No… I don’t think I can say every day. That wouldn’t be honest.

But there are times, after I eat too much or feel like I’ve eaten too much, when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, but that’s what happens. I get frightened that the food is going to stay in me, and then I feel like I have to do something right then, like I can’t just sit with it.

And when I don’t make myself vomit, I’ve also taken laxatives for that same reason. It’s all tied to that fear that the food is still inside me and I need to get it out somehow. But if you mean literally every single day, no, not every day.
